The table lists their marginal gains in expected spread under the independent cascade model, 1.37 for D and 1.17 for G, for an expected spread of 2.54." width="100%"} Uses a greedy algorithm to select seed nodes that maximize the expected spread in an Independent Cascade model. Useful for identifying key regulatory genes or optimal drug targets in signaling networks. In the Independent Cascade model, the seed nodes start out active. Each newly activated node gets a single chance to activate each of its inactive neighbors, succeeding with probability `probability=`, and the cascade continues until no new node is activated. The spread of a seed set is the expected number of active nodes at the end (seeds included), estimated by averaging `n_simulations=` random cascades. The greedy search adds one seed at a time, always choosing the node that raises the estimated spread the most. Typical uses: - choosing a small set of nodes from which information, influence, or a perturbation would reach the most of the network - ranking candidate intervention points (e.g., drug targets) by their downstream reach - comparing simulated reach with simpler heuristics such as picking the highest-degree nodes Because of the greedy strategy, two seeds placed in the same dense region are rarely chosen together: the second one would mostly reach nodes the first already covers. In directed graphs activation only travels along edge direction. Edge weights are not used; every edge has the same activation probability. The search runs about `k * n_nodes * n_simulations` cascades, so it becomes slow on large graphs; lower `n_simulations=` for a rough answer or restrict the analysis to a subgraph. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of seed nodes to select. If it exceeds the number of nodes, every node is selected; `k=0` returns an empty result. [model]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["independent_cascade"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Diffusion model. Currently only `"independent_cascade"` (the default) is supported. [probability]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.1]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Per-edge activation probability in each cascade step, between `0.0` and `1.0`. The default is `0.1`. Low values keep cascades local, so seeds with many direct neighbors win; high values let cascades run across the network, so the seeds' positions matter more than their degree. [n_simulations]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of Monte Carlo simulations per candidate evaluation. The default is `100`. Higher values give more stable estimates of the gains at a proportional cost in run time. Must be at least `1`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for reproducibility. With the default, `None`, the cascades (and possibly the selected nodes, when candidates are close) vary between calls. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return a list of `(node_id, marginal_gain)` tuples. If `False` (the default), return `self` for chaining. The selection is not written to the node table in that case, so use `return_dict=True` whenever you need the result. The call is still listed by `describe()`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph | list[tuple[int, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The selected seed nodes with their marginal gains (if `return_dict=True`) or `self`. The list is in selection order. The gain for the first node is the expected spread of that node on its own; each later gain is the estimated increase in expected spread from adding that node, so the gains add up to roughly the expected spread of the full seed set. Gains are Monte Carlo estimates and carry some noise. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `model=` is not `"independent_cascade"`, `probability=` is outside `[0, 1]`, or `n_simulations=` is `0`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} This graph has a four-spoke star around `Hub` and a separate three-node path. With `k=2`, the greedy search first picks `Hub`, then picks the middle of the path rather than a spoke, since a spoke would mostly reach nodes `Hub` already covers: ::: {#4d6f5b41 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph() g.add_nodes(["Hub", "A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G"]) g.add_edges( [("Hub", "A"), ("Hub", "B"), ("Hub", "C"), ("Hub", "D"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "G")] ) seeds = g.influence_maximization( k=2, probability=0.5, n_simulations=500, seed=42, return_dict=True ) [(g.get_label_from_id(node_id), round(gain, 2)) for node_id, gain in seeds] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [('Hub', 2.96), ('F', 1.87)] ``` ::: ::: In a directed chain, influence can only flow forward. With `probability=1.0` every activation succeeds, so the start of the chain reaches all four nodes: ::: {#3969368f .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} d = ec.Graph(directed=True) d.add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) d.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) seeds = d.influence_maximization(k=1, probability=1.0, seed=1, return_dict=True) [(d.get_label_from_id(node_id), gain) for node_id, gain in seeds] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [('A', 4.0)] ``` ::: :::
